## Presentation ≠ a research paper {.smaller}
::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
🚫 (Research Paper)

* Background 
* Methodology 
* Analysis 
* Results 
* Conclusions 

> This structure hides the most important information until the end, when you will typically have lost the attention of your audience 
  
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
✅ (Presentation)

* Recommendation - what should we do?
* Key insight – why should we do it?
* Supporting evidence – how do we know?
* Next steps – how do we start?

> Start with what matters most (lead statement), everything else is supporting material. Conclusion is the beginning of your presentation! 

:::
:::::

## Recorded Presentation Suggested Structure {.smaller}

* **Introduction/elevator pitch:** Begin with a captivating opening statement to grab the audience’s attention. Why should they care? 
* **Clearly define the problem or context** your data story addresses and explain its significance
* Present your **essential insights or findings** related to your topic (2 key visualisations) 
* Discuss **practical solutions, recommendations, or strategies** based on the data story and insights presented 
* Summarise the main points of your presentation and leave the audience with a **clear call to action or thought-provoking closing statement**
